oi.heading: Operating Income
oi.text:
Operating income decreased 13% in the third quarter and 6% in the four months ended September 30, 2026, primarily due to increased separation and other expenses related to IT and other professional services following the Spin-Off, increased salaries and employee benefit expenses, and increased operating supplies and expenses. These impacts were partially offset by increased revenue.

Salaries and employee benefits increased 4% in the third quarter and 5% in the four months ended September 30, 2026, primarily due to investments in our employees, including higher wage rates and increased variable incentive compensation.

Operating supplies and expenses increased 16% in the third quarter and in the four months ended September 30, 2026, primarily due to higher costs related to outside service contracts, professional fees, incremental software license costs, and other technology-related expenditures to support the business as a stand-alone company. Higher fuel expense also contributed to the increase in both periods.

Purchased transportation expense increased 18% in the third quarter and 17% in the four months ended September 30, 2026, primarily due to higher base rates and fuel prices.

nonop.heading: Other Income (Expense)
nonop.text: Other income (expense) changed unfavorably 149% in the third quarter and in the four months ended September 30, 2026 primarily due to the termination of the cash pooling arrangement associated with the Spin-Off, resulting in no related-party interest income in the third quarter and in the four months ended September 30, 2026, and higher third-party interest expense resulting from debt incurred during calendar year 2026.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text: Our effective tax rate was 27.5% for the third quarter and 27.5% for the four months ended September 30, 2026, compared to 25.5% for the third quarter and 25.6% for the four months ended September 30, 2025. The effective tax rates for the third quarter and four months ended September 30, 2026 were higher than the comparable prior-year periods primarily due to incremental nondeductible costs incurred in connection with operating as a stand-alone company. The effective tax rate exceeds the federal statutory rate primarily due to state taxes and non-deductible items.

net.text: The following tables compare revenue, operating expenses, operating income (dollars in millions), net income, operating expenses as a percent of revenue, operating margin, and selected statistics:

ocf.text: Cash Provided by Operating Activities. Cash flows from operating activities decreased $695 million in the four months ended September 30, 2026 primarily due to lower net income and working capital changes, driven by a decrease in intercompany amounts due to Parent related to the termination of the Company's factoring agreement with FedEx in preparation for the Spin-Off. For additional information regarding our historical factoring agreement with FedEx, refer to Note 1 2 , Related Party Transactions , of the accompanying financial statements.

net sales.heading: Revenue
net sales.text:
Revenue increased 8% in the third quarter and 9% in the four months ended September 30, 2026, primarily due to higher fuel surcharges and favorable base yield, partially offset by lower volume. Revenue for the four months ended September 30, 2026 was also positively affected by one additional operating day.

Revenue per shipment increased 10% and revenue per hundredweight increased 9% in both the third quarter and in the four months ended September 30, 2026, reflecting higher fuel surcharges, favorable base yield, and increased weight per shipment. Average daily shipments decreased 1% in each of the third quarter and the four months ended September 30, 2026 due to reduced demand for our services, primarily resulting from macroeconomic conditions.

Economy.text: While broader freight conditions have shown signs of improvement and volume and base yield trends continue to stabilize, we expect softness in the industrial economy to continue to put pressure on demand for LTL services for the remainder of calendar year 2026. We will continue to execute on our four key priorities of optimizing our network, strengthening our commercial offering, advancing our technology capabilities, and driving financial value creation.

Other.heading: Other Income (Expense)
Other.text: Other income (expense) changed unfavorably 149% in the third quarter and in the four months ended September 30, 2026 primarily due to the termination of the cash pooling arrangement associated with the Spin-Off, resulting in no related-party interest income in the third quarter and in the four months ended September 30, 2026, and higher third-party interest expense resulting from debt incurred during calendar year 2026.

intro.text: Headquartered in Memphis, Tennessee, FedEx Freight is the largest North American less-than-truckload (“LTL”) freight carrier, with industry-leading transit times and service levels, offering choice, simplicity, and reliability to meet the needs of LTL shippers while operating ethically with a commitment to “Safety Above All.” As of June 1, 2026, we had approximately 40,000 employees, over 365 locations, including approximately 355 shipping terminals (over 320 of which are in the United States) and approximately 10 linehaul relay sites, and nearly 30,000 motorized vehicles, of which nearly 17,000 are tractors, across all 50 U.S. states, Canada, and Mexico. We also offer freight delivery service to most points in Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
